title: Some Reformed, with Chamier, may reserve latria and dulia as names of different kinds, not degrees
source_text: XIX. Theologi tamen Reformati nonnulli testantur sibi non incommodum videri, si Latriae vox divino cultui reservetur, tanquam illi propria; honori vero & observantiae qua creaturae colendae sunt, singulariter aptetur vox Dulia, illique a divino & religioso cultu distinguendo inserviat. Id videre est apud Chamierum. Postquam enim pro certo constituit cultum Religiosum in solidum Deo concedendum, civilem vero ad creaturas pertinere: addit huic rei significandae nos uti posse vocabulis δουλείας & λατρείας: dummodo sciamus non esse ea nomina diversorum graduum, quasi secundum plus & minus, sed diversorum generum: ut omnino diversi sit generis cultus religiosus & cultus civilis, neque συνώνυμα neque ἀνάλογα ambo inter se comparari. Panstratia tom. 2. lib. 19. cap. 1. num. 11.
pass_a_gloss: Yet some Reformed theologians testify that it does not seem inconvenient to them if the word Latria is reserved to the divine cult as proper to it, and the word Dulia is singularly fitted to the honor and observance by which creatures are to be cultivated, and serves to distinguish that from the divine and religious cult. This may be seen in Chamier. For after he has established for certain that the religious cult is to be granted wholly to God, and the civil cult belongs to creatures, he adds that to signify this we can use the words douleia and latreia, provided we know that they are not names of different degrees, as if according to more and less, but of different kinds: so that the religious cult and the civil cult are altogether of a different kind, and the two are to be compared with each other neither as synonyms nor as analogues. Panstratia, volume 2, book 19, chapter 1, number 11.
pass_b_english: Some Reformed writers will still keep Latria for God's cult and Dulia for creature-honor, as a useful distinction.
Chamier allows the Greek words only if they name different kinds, not higher and lower degrees.
Religious cult and civil cult are not synonyms and not analogues of one another.

choices.why: Chamier refuses even analogy between the two cults, stronger than a mere verbal caution.
